catalogo.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), «Candidate rotations» and «Hard filters»; data dossier 27, §2.3 (INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017). The primary sources are given in each option and each filter

secuencia.fuente: INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017: planting from Sep 15 to Oct 31 (Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026))

indicadores.fuente: Legume: botanical classification of alfalfa (not from the master document). The rest: no data in the master document

alfalfa.por_que_en: Current rotation. Alfalfa is kept for 3–4 years; INIFAP reports 170–180 cm of irrigation per year in Chihuahua.
alfalfa.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), «typical current»; INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017 (170–180 cm of irrigation per year; 40 cm to establish)

indicadores.fuente: No data in the master document

nogal.por_que_en: An orchard does not rotate. Minimum-irrigation scenarios are the ones that apply, and kernel filling (August–September) should not be put at risk.
nogal.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), «Pecan»: does not rotate; ~1.5–1.82 m of irrigation; do not put kernel filling at risk (Aug–Sep)

secuencia.fuente: SDR Chihuahua, Mar 3, 2026: chile from February in the south-central region (data dossier 27, §2.3); it is a practice, not an absence of frost risk. No closing date in the sources

indicadores.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026): chile followed by bare fallow from Nov to Mar; «much bare soil»

chile.por_que_en: Current rotation. Chile followed by bare fallow from November to March leaves the soil uncovered in the windy season.

secuencia.fuente: INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017: Southeast–Delicias, from Apr 1 to May 10 (optimal from Apr 20 to 30) (Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026))

indicadores.fuente: No data in the master document

algodon.por_que_en: Current rotation. INIFAP reports about 68 cm of irrigation for cotton in Delicias; stalks must be destroyed before November 30.
algodon.fuente: INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017: ~68 cm (20 cm pre-planting irrigation + 48 cm in 4–5 supplementary irrigations); NOM-026 (Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option C)

secuencia.fuente: INIFAP, Folleto Técnico 53 (2014): irrigated spring planting from Apr 1 to May 31 (Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026))

indicadores.fuente: No data in the master document

maiz_forrajero.por_que_en: Current rotation. INIFAP reports 5 irrigations of 10–12 cm (50–60 cm in total) for spring forage maize in Chihuahua.
maiz_forrajero.fuente: INIFAP, Folleto Técnico 53 (2014) (Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option A)

secuencia.fuente: No sorghum planting date in the master document or in data dossier 27

indicadores.fuente: No data in the master document

sorgo.por_que_en: Current rotation. The project documents give no local planting date or irrigation depth for sorghum.
sorgo.fuente: Current crop seen by the A4 rules (crop map). The master document §5.2 and data dossier 27 give no sorghum planting date or irrigation depth; the depth is the demand model's (A5)

secuencia.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option A: autumn–winter oats or triticale, «Nov–Dec»; winter irrigation in Delicias not verified. The demand model plants on Dec 1 (midpoint of the window) [S]

indicadores.fuente: No data in the master document

cereal_invierno.por_que_en: Current rotation. Irrigated winter oats or triticale are not verified for Delicias; the single depth found (about 54 cm) comes from La Laguna.
cereal_invierno.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option A: ~54 cm (Ochoa-Espinoza 2022, La Laguna, not Delicias)

secuencia.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option A: autumn–winter oats or triticale, «Nov–Dec»; winter irrigation in Delicias not verified. The demand model plants on Dec 1 (midpoint of the window) [S]
INIFAP, Folleto Técnico 53 (2014): irrigated spring planting from Apr 1 to May 31 (Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026))

INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017: planting from Sep 15 to Oct 31 (Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026)); alfalfa is sown again after a year, with at least 12 months between stands

indicadores.fuente: No data in the master document for this sequence

avena_maiz.por_que_en: Suggested for an old alfalfa stand: one year of winter cereal and forage maize before sowing alfalfa again, because alfalfa should not follow alfalfa for at least 12 months.
avena_maiz.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option A; forage maize: INIFAP, Folleto Técnico 53 (2014); winter cereal ~54 cm: Ochoa-Espinoza 2022 (La Laguna, not Delicias)
avena_maiz.etiqueta: [V] forage maize and alfalfa; assumption [S] irrigated winter cereal in Delicias

alfalfa_corte_verano.nombre_en: Keep the alfalfa and skip two to three summer irrigations

secuencia.fuente: Nothing is planted: the established alfalfa is kept

indicadores.fuente: Legume: botanical classification of alfalfa (not from the master document)

alfalfa_corte_verano.por_que_en: Keeps the stand and plans a summer rest: 2–3 irrigations are skipped between July and September. Trials report that yield always drops and that stand survival depends on the soil.
alfalfa_corte_verano.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option B (moderate variant, update of Oct 29): INIFAP La Laguna 2008; UC ANR 8522 (2015); Bali et al. 2024. Trials from other regions; no published trial in DR-005
alfalfa_corte_verano.etiqueta: [V] trials from other regions; assumption [S] for DR-005

cereal_algodon.nombre_en: Break the chile cycle: winter cereal, then cotton

secuencia.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option A: autumn–winter oats or triticale, «Nov–Dec»; winter irrigation in Delicias not verified. The demand model plants on Dec 1 (midpoint of the window) [S]

indicadores.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option C: P. capsici is managed by rotation (INIFAP; Silva-Rojas et al. 2009)

cereal_algodon.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option C: INIFAP («do not plant chile after chile»); Silva-Rojas et al. 2009 (Delicias and Camargo); cotton: INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017
cereal_algodon.etiqueta: [V] rotation rule and cotton; assumption [S] irrigated winter cereal in Delicias

descanso.por_que_en: Intended for the worst water-supply scenario (option E of the master document): the field rests with standing stubble, which needs no irrigation and protects the soil against erosion. The master document lists low income as the risk of this option and gives no figure for it.
descanso.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option E («worst scenario»: «the rest rests with standing stubble»; supporting data «less demand; protects against erosion»; risk «low income», with no figure); no irrigation: rotaciones.json (A5), zero depth

regla.ventana_por_cultivo: the one in «secuencia.siembra» of each option (MM-DD)

filtros.texto_en: Planting must fall inside the window reported for the crop.

texto_por_opcion_en.cereal_sorgo: No local planting window was found for sorghum, so this rule checks the winter cereal and not the sorghum.

filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 1 (INIFAP planting dates by crop)

regla.nota: the master document sets no threshold: the frost probability of heladas.json for the planting date is shown and nothing is decided

filtros.texto_en: Chile planted from February is exposed to late frost. The card shows the chance of frost after the planting date; it does not decide.
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 2; probability computed with NASA POWER (heladas.json). INEGI 1983: last frost in March and earliest in November
filtros.etiqueta: [V] rule; the probability is for a regional grid cell, not a station

filtros.texto_en: Do not plant chile after chile. After a Phytophthora capsici outbreak, keep at least 5 years without host crops. The satellite memory shows summer crops but not which crop, so this needs a local check.
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 3: Silva-Rojas et al. 2009 (Delicias and Camargo; the stricter criterion is adopted); INIFAP gives 4 years

filtros.texto_en: Cotton stalks must be shredded within 10 days after harvest and uprooted before November 30 (official plant-health rule NOM-026).
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 4; INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017 (NOM-026)

regla.nota: compared live with the chosen allocation; 40 cm = 4 thousand m³/ha just to establish the alfalfa

filtros.texto_en: Alfalfa should not be established in a dry year: it needs about 40 cm of irrigation just to establish.
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 5; INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017 (40 cm in five irrigations of 8 cm)

filtros.texto_en: Leave at least 12 months between one alfalfa stand and the next (autotoxicity).
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 6. Fundación Produce Chihuahua gives a minimum of 6–7 months (secondary source); the stricter value is adopted

regla.unidad: ECe en dS/m; pérdida en % por cada dS/m por encima del umbral
regla.nota: oats and triticale have no numeric threshold in FAO-29 («moderately tolerant»). The ECe of the soil is not the EC of the irrigation water

filtros.texto_en: Salt tolerance differs by crop (FAO thresholds for soil salinity). There is no measured soil salinity for this field, so this needs a local check.
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 7: FAO-29, Table 4 (ECe threshold of the soil saturation extract, dS/m, and yield loss per dS/m above it); values from S2 §3, which the master document declares current. Cotton, wheat and barley: list of the same filter

filtros.texto_en: If atrazine was used on the previous maize or sorghum, labels ask to wait 5–10 months depending on the next crop and not to sow alfalfa. Check the label of the exact product.
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), filter 8: Mexican atrazine labels (Tridente and ADAMA), verified in S2 §3

filtros.texto_en: For an established stand; never in its year of establishment.
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option B: offered for an established alfalfa stand, never in its year of establishment

filtros.texto_en: Skipping summer irrigations is reasonable on deep, non-sandy soil without high salinity, and not elsewhere; risk is high on heavy clay under extreme heat. Soil texture and salinity are not measured for this field: needs a local check.
filtros.fuente: Project master document, §5.2 (v3.1, Oct 29, 2026), option B and its update of Oct 29 (Bali et al. 2024; UC ANR 8522)

opciones_del_maestro_no_entregadas.D_avena_veza: Option D of the master document (autumn–winter oat–vetch). Not delivered: the demand model (A5) has no sourced crop coefficient for the mix, and the master document marks seed, buyer and calendar in Delicias as not verified.
opciones_del_maestro_no_entregadas.E_sorgo_con_1_2_auxilios: Option E of the master document (sorghum with 1–2 supplementary irrigations). Not delivered as such: A5 computes sorghum with its full demand and the sources give no depth for a supplementary sorghum irrigation. The part «the rest rests with standing stubble» is the «descanso» option.

requisitos.fuente: FAO ECOCROP (species sheets, ecocrop.apps.fao.org) and FAO Land & Water («Crop information») for pH and texture; FAO-29, Table 4, for salinity (via opciones_b3.json); Gutiérrez González et al. (2022) for pecan nutrients. All read on Nov 14, 2026; each block with its link
requisitos.nota: GENERAL worldwide ranges: they are not trials in DR-005. Several crops grown in the area fall outside their general pH range at the map pH (~8.1); the soil map is a 250 m model. Do not use it as a filter that rules options out: it is one more piece of evidence

grupos_textura.fuente: Own split of the 12 USDA texture classes into the light, medium and heavy groups of ECOCROP; the ECOCROP sheet does not define its groups

nutrientes.texto_en: Soil tests from pecan orchards in this irrigation district (2018–2021) found most soils low in nitrogen, phosphorus, zinc, iron and copper, and most soils alkaline. This is a district-wide finding, not a measurement of this field: it needs a soil test.
nutrientes.fuente: Gutiérrez González, L.S. et al. (2022), «Análisis del suelo y su importancia en el cultivo del nogal pecanero en el Distrito de Riego 05 Delicias», Revista Biológico Agropecuaria Tuxpan 10(1), DOI 10.47808/revistabioagro.v10i1.395 (abstract at https://agris.fao.org/search/en/records/67598d78c7a957febdfbf098, read on Nov 14, 2026): soil analyses from 2018 to May 2021 of orchards in Delicias, Saucillo, Meoqui, Rosales and Julimes; «solo el 14% de los suelos tienen un pH de 6.7 a 7.3» (14 % of the soils have a pH of 6.7 to 7.3), the rest is alkaline, and «la mayoría de los suelos presentan concentraciones bajas de nitrógeno, fosforo, zinc, hierro y cobre» (most soils have low concentrations of nitrogen, phosphorus, zinc, iron and copper)
nutrientes.etiqueta: [V] article abstract; no figures per field

textura.etiqueta: [V] groups of the source; split into USDA classes assumption [S]

cereal_invierno.nota: oats and triticale have no numeric threshold in FAO-29 («moderately tolerant»). The ECe of the soil is not the EC of the irrigation water

sin_requisitos.forraje_verano: grouped map class (forage maize or sorghum): use maiz_forrajero or sorgo

supuestos._encabezado: AI-assisted (Claude Code) — ROOT, NASA Space Apps 2026
supuestos._nota: Assumptions of the data pieces. Each value carries a source and a label; [S] = assumption. The scripts stop if a key is missing. Copy to the working folder (--dir).

ea_gravedad.fuente: No value measured in DR-005 and no source in the repository; sensitivity range proposed by the team

sesgo_eto.fuente: No source in the repository; it tests the hypothesis that POWER-PM overestimates ETo by up to 10 %

presiembra_mm.fuente: Team kit (document 40), A5: pre-planting irrigation of 15–20 cm

plazo_alfalfa_anios.fuente: FIRA AGROCOSTOS 2025: productive life of 3–4 years

plazo_nogal_horizonte.fuente: S9 §5: calculation horizon, not the life of the orchard; the orchard age is not subtracted

umbral_verde_ndvi.fuente: S9 §5; sensitivity 0.35–0.45; to be calibrated with blind labels

umbral_invierno_nogal.fuente: Labeling manual (document 39): dormant pecan 0.10–0.22 in December; margin up to 0.30

viento_alto.fuente: Percentile of ws2m (Feb–Apr 1981–2025) that defines a high-wind day; no published threshold for Delicias

umbral_ruta_ha.fuente: Display value for drawing runoff routes

prof_depresion_ruta_m.fuente: Fill depth above which no route is drawn: above the vertical noise of NASADEM (1–3 m per cell), the elevation model shows a closed depression and does not tell where the water leaves

elevacion_punto_m.fuente: No source in the repository; assumption. The NASADEM median of the area is 1,201 m in Delicias–Saucillo and 1,194 m in Lázaro Cárdenas (nasadem_zona_piloto.tif); with them the psychrometric constant of FAO-56 would change by 0.3 % or less, so the value was not replaced

presiembra_algodon_mm.fuente: No source in the repository; upper end of the range of the team kit

kc_nogal_tabla.fuente: FAO-56, Tabla 12, renglón «Walnut orchard» (Kc ini, mid, end)

cobertura_dosel_nogal.fuente: Effective canopy cover fraction; to be measured with the NDVI of the pecan fields (S8, decision 5). The estimate from NDVI is in nogal_referencia

altura_nogal_m.fuente: Typical height of an adult orchard; it enters FAO-56 Eq. 98

corte_verano_moderado.etiqueta: [P] team kit B3 (skip 2–3 irrigations between July and September); riegos_jul_sep = 6 assumption [S]
corte_verano_moderado.fuente: Team kit (document 40), B3: moderate variant by default

umbral_resiembra_ndvi.fuente: Lowest monthly NDVI of the year below which the field is taken as bare (reseeding or establishment of the alfalfa); in the pilot area, established alfalfa stands have yearly minimums of 0.26 or more and establishment years 0.12–0.24. Sensitivity 0.20–0.30

ea_goteo.fuente: FAO, Irrigation Water Management Training Manual No. 4, «Irrigation Scheduling» (Brouwer, Prins and Heibloem, 1989), Annex I, Table 8 «Indicative values of the field application efficiency (ea)»: surface irrigation 60 %, sprinkler 75 %, drip 90 %. https://www.fao.org/3/t7202e/t7202e08.htm, read on Nov 14, 2026. General indicative value, not measured in DR-005

ea_superficial_referencia.fuente: FAO, Irrigation Water Management Training Manual No. 4, «Irrigation Scheduling» (Brouwer, Prins and Heibloem, 1989), Annex I, Table 8 «Indicative values of the field application efficiency (ea)»: surface irrigation 60 %, sprinkler 75 %, drip 90 %. https://www.fao.org/3/t7202e/t7202e08.htm, read on Nov 14, 2026. General indicative value, not measured in DR-005. A reference: the calculation uses the range of ea_gravedad

gedi_piso_instrumento_m.fuente: Own analysis (datos/colab/A11_gedi_parcelas.py, Nov 14, 2026): 10th and 90th percentiles (value = median) of the per-field median rh98 in the 261 fields with 3 or more shots that the rules classify as alfalfa, fallow or winter cereal (no trees). Below that level rh98 reflects the pulse width of the instrument, not plant height

min_disparos.fuente: Minimum valid shots per field to read the height; own criterion

gedi_umbral_dosel_alto_m.fuente: Own criterion (A11, Nov 14, 2026): 90th percentile of the field's rh98 of 5 m or more. With that threshold, 57 of 86 pecan fields with 3 or more shots show tall canopy, against 7 of 95 alfalfa fields and 0 of 11 winter cereal fields

lamina_local_cm._nota: Published irrigation depths for the region, in cm per year or per cycle. They are a REFERENCE to compare with the model depth; the calculation does not use them. 10 cm = 1 thousand m³/ha

recomendada_inifap.fuente: INIFAP, Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Chihuahua 2017 (verified in the project dossier, S2 §3): 170–180 cm per year

aplicada_dr005.fuente: Villalobos-Cano et al. 2024, Sustainability 16(5):1851, DOI 10.3390/su16051851, Tables 2 and 3: DR-005, means for 2009–2016 (verified in the project dossier, S2 §3, Oct 29, 2026). The article does not say where the applied water was measured and computes ET with Hargreaves; it serves as a contrast, not as a calibration

INIFAP, Folleto Técnico 53 (2014): 5 irrigations of 10–12 cm, including pre-planting (project master document, §5.2)

cobertura_ndvi_relacion.etiqueta: [V] published relation; assumption [S] when applied to adult pecan orchards
cobertura_ndvi_relacion.fuente: Johnson, L.F. and Trout, T.J. (2012), Remote Sensing 4(2):439–455, DOI 10.3390/rs4020439, Eq. 1: Fc = 1.26 × NDVI − 0.18 (r² = 0.96; Landsat NDVI; vegetables, vineyards and young orchards of the San Joaquin Valley; the authors did not verify it in adult orchards). Read on Nov 14, 2026. Used in A12 as a reference; the demand calculation does not use it

nogal_referencia._nota: REFERENCE on the pecan orchards of the pilot areas (A12, Nov 14, 2026). The demand calculation does not use this block: A5 keeps cobertura_dosel_nogal. Details in docs/nogal_cobertura.md

cobertura_estimada_ndvi.fuente: Median and 10th and 90th percentiles of 105 fields classified as pecan in the two areas: maximum NDVI of Jun–Sep 2026 (NASA HLS) converted to cover with cobertura_ndvi_relacion. Consistent with the model's assumption (cobertura_dosel_nogal = 0.7)

kc_mid_estimado.fuente: FAO-56, Eq. 98 with kc_nogal_tabla and altura_nogal_m, applied to the estimated cover of each field (before the climate adjustment). The model uses 1.07

lamina_bruta_millares_ha_p50.fuente: P50 gross irrigation depth of pecan in Delicias–Saucillo (A5) with the cover at the estimated 10th and 90th percentiles (0.57 and 0.83) and with the model's cover (0.7). Range by cover; it does not include the P10–P90 band of climate and efficiency

altura_gedi_p90_m.fuente: Median and 10th and 90th percentiles, among 86 pecan fields with 3 or more GEDI shots, of the 90th percentile of rh98 of each field. The model assumes 10 m (altura_nogal_m); with 7 m the mid-season Kc changes in the second decimal

parcelas_con_patron_huerta_2016_2026.fuente: Of 105 pecan fields, those that show the orchard pattern in all 11 years of the HLS memory (2016–2026): they are at least 11 years old

edad_promedio_huertas_encuesta_anios.fuente: Orona Castillo, I. et al. (2019), «La producción y comercialización de nuez pecanera en México», Revista Mexicana de Ciencias Agrícolas 10(8):1797–1808 (INIFAP journal; https://cienciasagricolas.inifap.gob.mx/index.php/agricolas/article/download/1833/2842/11310), read on Nov 14, 2026: «La edad de los huertos es similar en las tres zonas (27 años en promedio)» (orchard age is similar in the three areas, 27 years on average); surveys of 2014–2015 in the Comarca Lagunera, Jiménez (Chihuahua) and Hermosillo (Sonora). It is not Delicias and it is not the life of the orchard

edad_arboles_unidad_tipica_delicias_anio.fuente: López Díaz, J.C. et al. (2011), «Rentabilidad del nogal pecanero bajo sistemas de producción de mediana tecnología en Delicias, Chihuahua», Revista Mexicana de Agronegocios 29:720–731 (https://ageconsearch.umn.edu/record/114475), read on Nov 14, 2026: typical unit with «árboles con madurez de producción comercial (25 años de edad)» (trees at commercial production maturity, 25 years old). It is not an INIFAP publication and it is not the life of the orchard

vida_huerta_anios.fuente: No INIFAP publication giving the life of the orchard in years was found (search of Nov 14, 2026). No figure is published; what does have a source is the age of orchards in production (see the two previous entries)

suelo_margen_ph.fuente: Own criterion (Nov 14, 2026): a pH difference smaller than this margin between the map and the published limit of a crop is not labeled «outside range» but «near the published limit». It does not come from a pH uncertainty figure: Table 4 of Poggio et al. 2021 (DOI 10.5194/soil-7-217-2021) is an image and could not be read; the text of the article gives model efficiencies (MEC) of 0.31 to 0.74 depending on the property, and ISRIC states that its models explain between 30 % and 70 % of the variation

suelo_coincidencia_textura.fuente: Share of fields where the USDA texture class computed from SoilGrids 2.0 (0–30 cm) equals the OpenLandMap one (0 cm): 584 of 1,238 fields with data in the two pilot areas; in the others they differ by a neighboring class

ecostress_sobrevuelo_seg.fuente: Scenes of the same field less than 5 minutes apart are one overpass and are averaged before the monthly median (in these files, three pairs of scenes 52 s apart: Dec 16, 2025, Feb 26 and Aug 26, 2026); independent review of Nov 15, 2026 (docs/revisiones/2026-11-15_ecostress.md, D5)

ecostress_fraccion_luz.fuente: Passes are used when x, the fraction of the daylight hours elapsed at the pass (0 at sunrise, 1 at sunset), is between these limits. The product turns the instantaneous flux into a daily total with 1.6 · Rn / (π · sin(π · x)) (JPL, github.com/ECOSTRESS-Collection-2/ECOv002-L3T-L4T-JET, ECOv002_L3T_L4T_JET.py, daily_Rn_integration_verma, commit a785b14, read on Nov 15, 2026), so near sunrise or sunset it multiplies a small, noisy flux by more than 2.2 times the noon factor; limits from the independent review of Nov 15, 2026 (docs/revisiones/2026-11-15_ecostress.md, D1)

ecostress_nube_zona_max.fuente: A scene is left out for a pilot area if more than this fraction of the area's points have cloud = 1 in it (May 20 and Jul 2, 2026: 49 % to 99 %; every other scene with data: 4 % or less). The product leaves cloudy pixels empty, so cloud = 0 alone does not remove a pass with half of the area under cloud; independent review of Nov 15, 2026 (docs/revisiones/2026-11-15_ecostress.md, D2)
